originalTitle: Steam Deck 2: Is AMD Gainsborough the chip Valve’s been waiting for?
summary: The Steam Deck is four and a half years old, and handheld gamers are eagerly awaiting a Steam Deck 2 - but Valve has consistently said it needs a new chip with a "generational leap" in performance and efficiency before building the sequel. content: The Steam Deck is four and a half years old, and handheld gamers are eagerly awaiting a Steam Deck 2 — but Valve has consistently said it needs a new chip with a “generational leap” in performance and efficiency before building the sequel. There’s some reason to believe that chip has now broken cover: AMD Gainsborough. But I’m a tad skeptical. As leaker Moore’s Law is Dead and IT Home report, the latest AMD drivers have leaked the codename for a previously unknown chip: an “AMD Gainsborough.” The first Steam Deck chip was named “Aerith” after Final Fantasy VII’s heartbreaking love interest, and Gainsborough is her last name. Plus, the chip appears to be a semi-custom one (read: designed for a specific customer) on TSMC’s relatively recent N3P process. [Media: https://youtu.be/3gy-dUHd-1s?si=FnNapGtIvPnfNyMw&t=139] IT Home checked import/export records and found that AMD’s already been shipping test equipment for the Gainsborough chip for validation, suggesting that a potential customer might already be testing to see if it’s suitable for their device. [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/fe78cc35-9834-437c-ad00-8a9d5d0eda01-1.jpg%40s_2w_820h_481.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] Those import records also show the Gainsborough chip will be fairly small, with an FF6 package measuring 25mm by 25mm. Today, leaker Gotou_3rd seemingly revealed that AMD’s next handheld chips, the Ryzen Z3 and Z3 Extreme, will also be 25mm by 25mm chips. Gotou also published a possible fragment of an AMD slide deck that suggests the Z3 is targeting 15 watts, the same power envelope as the Steam Deck and Steam Deck OLED: [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/AMD-RYZEN-Z3-RYZEN-Z3-EXTREME-LEAK-850x264-1.webp?quality=90&strip=all] This isn’t quite enough to tie Gainsborough specifically to a Steam Deck 2, though. First, a semi-custom chip doesn’t always wind up in its originally intended gadget. It’s long been rumored that the Steam Deck’s own semi-custom chip wasn’t originally designed for the Steam Deck, but rather a Magic Leap headset, and that it was shopped around for tablets (including this canceled Microsoft tablet, the story goes) before Valve took advantage. There are portions of the original Steam Deck’s chip that went entirely unused. Second, you should know that “Aerith” (Steam Deck), “Sephiroth” (Steam Deck OLED) and “Gainsborough” are not Valve’s codenames. When I visited Valve’s headquarters in late 2023, I commented on this Aerith wafer hanging on the wall — and Valve designers told me they didn’t really want the Final Fantasy codenames. AMD was the one that chose them. [Image: The Aerith wafer I saw at Valve HQ. https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/DJI_20231030165027_0123_D-1.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] Some extra evidence that Valve isn’t tied to those names: When Microsoft and Asus picked the “Ryzen Z2 A” chip for the vanilla $500 Xbox Ally, they were choosing an “Aerith Plus” chip. Third, 25mm by 25mm might be small, but it’s actually large for a Steam Deck! The original Steam Deck’s “Aerith” chip, before it shrunk to remove the unused components in its “Sephiroth” revision, reportedly measured 19mm by 19mm. But perhaps Gainsborough is efficient, and perhaps it’s more affordable if this apple doesn’t fall too far from AMD’s 25mm x 25mm Ryzen Z3 tree. Lastly, Valve was still figuring out “how and when” to do a Steam Deck 2 as of last month, after it would have theoretically received these Gainsborough chips. But I guess Valve might just be trying not to overpromise, after this year’s RAM-forced hardware delays.

chineseContent: Steam Deck 已有四年半的历史，掌上游戏玩家都在热切地等待 Steam Deck 2，但 Valve 一直表示，在开发续作之前，它需要一款在性能和效率上实现“代际飞跃”的新芯片。有一些理由相信该芯片现已揭开面纱：AMD Gainsborough。但我有点怀疑。正如泄密者《摩尔定律已死》和 IT Home 报道的那样，最新的 AMD 驱动程序泄露了一款以前未知的芯片的代号：“AMD Gainsborough”。第一个 Steam Deck 芯片以《最终幻想 VII》中令人心碎的恋人的名字命名为“Aerith”，Gainsborough 是她的姓氏。另外，该芯片似乎是采用台积电相对较新的 N3P 工艺的半定制芯片（即：为特定客户设计）。 [媒体：https://youtu.be/3gy-dUHd-1s?si=FnNapGtIvPnfNyMw&t=139] IT Home 检查了进出口记录，发现 AMD 已经在运送 Gainsborough 芯片的测试设备进行验证，这表明潜在客户可能已经在测试该芯片是否适合他们的设备。 [图片：https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/fe78cc35-9834-437c-ad00-8a9d5d0eda01-1.jpg%40s_2w_820h_481.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]这些导入记录还显示Gainsborough芯片将相当小， FF6 封装尺寸为 25mm x 25mm。今天，泄密者 Gotou_3rd 似乎透露 AMD 的下一代手持芯片 Ryzen Z3 和 Z3 Extreme 也将是 25mm x 25mm 芯片。 Gotou 还发布了 AMD 幻灯片的可能片段，表明 Z3 的目标功率为 15 瓦，与 Steam Deck 和 Steam Deck OLED 的功率范围相同：[图片： https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/AMD-RYZEN-Z3-RYZEN-Z3-EXTREME-LEAK-850x264-1.webp?quality=90&strip=all]这个
